From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Atlas RFP — follow-up on multi-region DR behavior

Jane, thanks — sending a targeted summary here and attaching the high-level runbook and the RTO/RPO matrix. If helpful we can also schedule a 30-minute technical deep-dive with our reliability team.

Executive summary (short bullets you can paste into the packet):
- Typical failover model we recommend: active-passive regional pair with automated health gating and canary traffic. Active-active is available for dedicated deployments with per-tenant cross-region replication (see matrix).
- Recovery Time Objective (RTO): Hosted API standard region failover target is 30 minutes for routing and service rehydration; Dedicated commitments can be configured to 15–30 minutes depending on reserved capacity and pre-warmed pools.
- Recovery Point Objective (RPO): For customer-owned persistent storage (S3/GCS) RPO is effectively zero (object writes durable). For in-service KV caches and ephemeral caches, practical RPO is up to 5–15 minutes depending on workload and selected cache durability settings.
- Data at risk: in-flight token-level state and per-request KV cache entries; model KV cache (per-session) is best-effort and may be lost during cross-region cutover unless you enable cross-region checkpointing (recommended for session-sensitive workloads).

Attached: a condensed runbook (Redwood_GeoFailure_Playbook_v2.pdf) and a per-deployment RTO/RPO matrix (RTO_RPO_matrix_AtlasBank.xlsx). Key excerpts below.

Excerpt: Switchover sequencing (high level)
1) Detect: region health summary from infra probes + customer SDK/agent pings (0s).
2) Validate: automatic health policy run — if >2 critical services fail for >60s, mark region degraded.
3) Pre-warm: spin up standby nodes in target region using reserved image + cache warmers (1–10m depending on instance pool).
4) Drain & redirect: stop accepting new long-running requests in degraded region, redirect new sessions to target region via edge routing and low TTL DNS (TTL=30s recommended) + CDN config updates (0–60s).
5) Rehydrate KV: stream persisted checkpoints to target region; apply incremental event logs to reach last known good state (this determines final RPO).
6) Canary: route 1–5% of production traffic and monitor latency/error budgets for 5–15 minutes.
7) Cutover: increase traffic gradually once canary passes.

Also noted constraints/variants:
- Hosted customers on multi-tenant pools: failover prioritizes availability; RPO may be higher for ephemeral caches (recommend retaining session state externally for strict RPO).
- Dedicated: can enable synchronous cross-region replication for critical state stores to target RPO <1s; requires additional config and reserved inter-region bandwidth (described in the attachment).

What we need from Atlas for a canary:
- A test tenant or header you can toggle so traffic is identifiable.
- Target failover window(s) and contact list for on-call support.
- Any regulatory blackout periods where switchover cannot be initiated.

I can join a call Wednesday afternoon (PDT) for the deep-dive.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Ethan — answers inline below and added a short rollback checklist.

Q1 — coverage by replication mode:
- Model artifacts (weights/checkpoints): stored in durable object storage with multi-region replication options; by default object writes are durable and considered available in target region once replication completes. For Dedicated customers we offer an optional synchronous replication mode for critical model stores (reduces RPO to near-zero but increases write latency).
- Embeddings & feature stores: typically backed by managed databases; read replicas and cross-region replication can be enabled. Default is asynchronous, RPO depends on replication lag (usually <30s with our recommended configuration).
- Request logs & telemetry: streamed to central telemetry pipeline (Kafka-like). By default these are eventually consistent; we support setting up mirrored pipelines to a secondary region for near-real-time duplication if required (enterprise add-on).

Q2 — canary rollback criteria (recommended):
- Immediate rollback if error rate >1.5% above baseline for p50 requests OR if p95 latency increases >40% versus baseline over a 5-minute sliding window.
- Soft rollback (reduce traffic) if error rate is 0.8–1.5% above baseline or p95 latency increase is 20–40% for 10 minutes.
- Stop test if any SLO for authentication or billing flows fails.

DNS handling for Hosted offering:
- Redwood manages automated edge routing and CDN config changes as part of our hosted failover. We do not require the customer to manually change provider records during a standard region cutover if you opt into our managed routing. We recommend TTL=30s for critical endpoints; TTLs longer than 60s increase failover time. For Dedicated/Private deployments we can coordinate with your DNS provider and hand off control if you require provider-side changes.

Rollback checklist (short):
1) Pause traffic shift, redirect new sessions back to source region.
2) Invalidate partial cache rehydrates in target region.
3) Re-run consistency checks versus object store snapshots.
4) Restore DNS/CDN if applicable and monitor for resumed baseline.

I'll attach a one-page rollback matrix into the Drive folder; happy to convert to your procurement template. Proposed next step: schedule the deep-dive and a table-top canary run (we'll provide a preflight checklist).

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
